Story Updates Sep 2019

By: Sophia Phirippides | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Over the year Carte Blanche has brought to light stories that affect the lives of ordinary South Africans but sometimes questions remain unanswered. We revisit some of them and give you an update.

Unique Selling Point:
Research has shown that Carte Blanche viewers want feedback on some stories that have been aired but may still have questions hanging. We revisit some of those stories and keep our viewers updated and engaged with our content.

Summary:
The stories we will revisit are as follows:

1. Dusi River Chemical disaster

Mark Graham from Ground Truth has been employed by Willowton to do an EIA after the chemical spillage, as Willowton have taken responsibility for the disaster, and are engaging in a rehabilitation process of the area. He will send us the update on the area.

2. Gluten free Bread

We go back to the two health shops featured in the story and see if they are labelling the bread differently, we also check on Dr Maimoona’s credentials that she touts as a naturopath.

3. Rape Kits

Women and men against child abuse are giving out rape comfort kits after the airing of our rape kit shortage story and they are delivering their first batch to the Alexandra Clinic in Alexandra. We will also follow up on the roll out of the actual rape kits throughout the country now that the tender has been awarded. This is within the backdrop of the GBV protests, and we can show the footage that Lezanne filmed in Sandton.

4. Lifestyle Legal

Currently the class action is being instituted against Lifestyle Legal by the Stellenboch Law Clinic. Stephan Van der Merwe will provide us with an update.

5. Chaos the lion

We go to the Centurion Zoo and Visit Chaos the Lion who has fully recovered from his cancer and speak to his owner, Matty Lory on his recovery.

6. Noni Tenge
Noni has just retained her WBF welterweight title, and now has her eye on the Olympics, but the Department of sport has not paid the outstanding amounts for her studies at UKZN as promised on camera to Carte Blanche. We try and get some clarity from the department.

Further information:
The links into the stories will be presented in a high tech way using a horizontal floating screen which has a visual block of each story, which can be tapped or swiped by the presenter and that will take us into the update.

Press Release:


This week in our extended broadcast Carte Blanche revisits several stories from the last year to find out if our truth has brought any change. We pick up the trail and answer some lingering questions.

Script:


1. ONLINE LOAN SCAM

LINK: In April this year we exposed an alleged online loan scam, where thousands of people presumed they were making simple loan applications but instead ended up paying for services they say, they didn't sign up for. But now hapless victims may have their day in court. (16")

VO: Our investigation led to one company - Lifestyle legal - remember Damien Malander, he was the man behind Lifestyle legal and the registered owner of 12 of the websites that appeared to offer loans and or free loan finding services?

None of the victims that contacted Carte Blanche ever received a loan through these websites. Instead they discovered they were locked into a subscription package for a year, for a variety of other services - including loan finding services.

Sound up: there I stopped, so I thought by not responding to the email, I'd killed the problem.
VO: For those who managed to cancel debit orders, they were inundated with a barrage of threatening sms', payment demands and additional legal fees from the collection company Lifestyle Legal, (16")

At the time Derek went on the hunt for Damien Malander the registered owner of Lifestyle Legal to get some answers, but he remained elusive. (8")

Sound up Derek and montage… no he's gone to the office, he's not here… etc (8")

VO: After our story, Stephan Van der Merwe of the Stellenbosch Law Clinic and eight of their clients filed an application at the Western Cape High Court instituting an opt-out class action lawsuit on behalf of thousands of allegedly duped consumers.

VO: Mr Malander did give a written response to Carte Blanche in our initial story denying all allegations. We tried to contact him again, to get comment on the class action lawsuit but as yet he has not responded.
(beat)
VO: In November this year, the applicants will seek an interdict to shut down the websites and restrain them from debiting bank accounts. Once the class has been approved summons will be issued against the websites and their operators in an attempt to get their money back. 15"


2. NONI TENGE

LINK: She is one of 5 women who motivated government to legalise female boxing in SA in 2001. At the age of 37 she had won 5 different world titles in various weight divisions. If you had never heard of Noni Tenge (she bee stinging), you did on Carte Blanche in january this year, on her comeback to the women's boxing scene. Looking to defend her Women's WBF Super Welterweight title Noni finally saw the inside of a ring again. So how did she do?
(28")
Sound up: Howard Goldberg. She's an icon blah blah…

VO: [ding ding] Noni successfully defended her World Boxing Federation title at the end of August, where she defeated Mapule Ngubane. (8")

VO: [ding ding] Another outstanding issue was Noni's university fees which were sponsored by the Department of Sport but had not been fully paid up, leaving Noni without her diploma in sport's management. Then Director General Alec Moemi, told Carte Blanche that he would ensure they honour their agreement. (16")

sound up (Comeback Noni)

Mac: So we get the documents you pay

DDG: Certainly no issue.

VO:[ding ding] But it seemed that the correct documents were not forthcoming from the University, until we made a check up call this week and the current Acting Director General of Sport and Recreation Sumayya Khan made it all happen and sent Carte Blanche proof of payment to confirm that Noni’s fees have now been settled. (24")

VO: Now Noni is pursuing her dream of representing South Africa at the Olympic Games as the rules on professional participation have changed. (9)"


3. CHAOS THE LION

LINK: A few months ago we came up close and personal with a 16 year old skin cancer patient - Chaos the lion from the Lory Park Zoo. He was diagnosed with cancerous lesions on his nose and foot. And In an unusual situation, he received radiation treatment from a human hospital, a South African first and Carte Blanche was there, but is he fully recovered? (22")

VO: Matty Van Eck is Chaos' co-owner, she said there was no other option as no veterinary practices had the appropriate equipment. (10")

Sound up Derek VO: carte blanche followed the 3rd of his 4 radiation treatments …. cost 50 000 rand … all the way to the darting of chaos with the doctor.. to that's what he thinks of me … it's a good shot (approximately 15")

VO: Chaos was treated successfully with radiation therapy and some of the tumors were surgically removed. (8")

Sound up Derek : A sigh of relief as Chaos blinks (5")

VO: It's been a few months since his harrowing ordeal and we paid Chaos a visit to see how he is faring . (8") He greeted his co-owner Matty Van Eck followed closely by his lifelong partner Tequila

Matty 00:02:16:09 – 00:02:35:25
Yes. So to protect the areas where had the treatment from the cancer reoccurring he's got to get sunblock every morning before he comes out. (11")

Mac 00:01:52:20 – 00:01:58:11
How's the treatment going. Matty 00:01:58:11 – 00:02:12:13
Matty: It was a difficult decision to make because we knew how much stress and how much he was gonna have to go through it was a good decision and a good outcome. He's really doing well. (19")

Mac [00:02:54.03]
and is enjoying himself here with his partner.
Matty 00:02:55:16 – 00:02:58:26
He is.
Mac [00:02:58.20]
Oh what's life without tequila?
Matty [00:02:59.13]
Exactly! (8")


4. RAPE KIT SHORTAGE

LINK: This year the rape statistics are grimmer than ever with 41 583 reported rapes, With such alarming figures, it was touted as a national crisis when in August, Carte Blanche broke the story on a shortage of evidence collection kits including sexual assault kits, otherwise known as rape kits at police stations, due to tenders that were not awarded. We keep track of the story.
(27")
VO: Two weeks later we reported that the tender had been awarded and a roll out plan was scheduled. Spokesperson for the National Commissioner of Police, Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo, gives us the current status. ( 11")
Vish 00:00:04:11 – 00:00:35:15
we're expecting the next delivery between the 14th and 18th of October and then followed by 27th of October to the 1st of November and then again from the 11th to the 15th of November for this year.
Mac 00:00:35:07 – 00:01:00:03
would that be enough to cover most of the police stations around the country or every police station around the country? (7")
Vish 00:01:00:03 – 00:01:27:26
As we stand now, we are fine. We have enough kits.
VO: But Brigadier Naidoo denies that there was ever a shortage of rape kits, and says that police stations were mandated to procure rape kits from other suppliers while the tender was being awarded.

Vish Naidoo: [00:12:11.07] So those figures that they were buying were not being fed into the central system. So they got the figures from that central system whereas the provinces physically had those collection kits.

VO: He also states that on the 5th of August an inventory was done by Major General LInda , Head of the FCS unit and there were enough rape kits around the country. This he says averaged around 45 kits per station, but the distribution is weighted to the more densely populated precincts.

Vish: [00:10:10.29] The turnaround time has to be quicker than in a rural area or outlying area. But having said that it does not mean that service delivery must be compromised.

VO: But our report told a different story. (11")

01: 46 Claire
A sexual assault kit like this can be the difference beween somebody being convicted and walking away scott free.
Sound up: Undercover person
01:22 there's units that don't have any rape kits.
Claire: Out of fear of reprisal FCS officer Thabo is hiding his identity to expose this critical shortage. Carte Blanche confirmed his story with other FCS officers and prosecutors.

Sound up undercover: 2:25 - We are struggling to get kits now for the past year, especially the buccal sample to compare the DNA that was found on the victim with a suspect.

VO: Brigadier Naidoo, does agree that there was a shortage of buccal swab kits, but he says, the same outcome can be achieved through taking blood samples. (12"))
Vish 00:05:19:01 – 00:06:22:01
In fact that is about the first evidence collection kit that we have already taken delivery of. (13")
(Beat)
VO: Our story had a profound impact on one of our viewers, Penny Stein who together with the Angel Network raised R240 000 and created a rape comfort kit for victims, which includes soft toys for children and hygene products. Last week they made their first delivery at the Alexandra Clinic in Sandton. 10"


5 LIVE ANIMAL EXPORTS

LINK: A few weeks ago we did an expose on the cruel conditions surrounding the transportation of livestock by sea to the Middle East from Australia. But now the company Al Mawashi who was responsible for these inhumane conditions is on South African shores and has secured a deal to ship millions of our sheep live - to the Middle East over the next few years. Will our government allow this practice to continue? (25")
Sound up: Shatha Hamade
The inherent suffering and risk in this trade are actually unavoidable. (5")
VO: Docked on our shores The Al Shuwaikh, Al Mawashi's Cargo ship is now waiting for roughly 61 000 sheep, destined for a traumatic journey to the Middle East. (9")
In our story we reported that Senior Inspector Nazareth Appalsamy with the NSPCA’s Farm Animal Protection Unit met with a representative from Al Mawashi earlier this year.(9")

Sound Up Inspector: Shockingly he told us that they intend importing over the next three to 5 years 600,000 animals annually made up of sheep, goats and cattle. (9")

VO: Carte Blanche had gained access to undercover footage onboard export vessels, including the Al Shuwaikh, that is so disturbing we decided it unsuitable for broadcast.
sound up -[Sheep insert: 02:52] It shows sheep weak from heat exhaustion, collapsing and literally drowning in their own waste
VO: Last Sunday the NSPCA undertook an inspection of the empty Al-Shuweikh vessel, and found it to be unsuitable to transport 61 000 sheep.
Two inspections this week at Al-Mawashi's sheep feedlot on Page Farming Trust premises in Berlin, Eastern Cape, found a number of serious concerns. Sheep were fighting over food and no shelter was provided, amongst other cruel conditions. The Inspectors had to euthanase a total of seven sheep.
VO: We tried to contact Al-Mawashi for comment on the inspections but they did not answer our calls. We were told the owners of Page Farming Trust were out of the country and unavailable for comment.
The NSPCA have appealed to the South African Government to take a stand against the export of live sheep to Kuwait. (37").


6. GLUTEN FREE FOOD

LINK: Gluten has become a no no in many diets, and many people claim to be gluten intolerant, so they opt for foods - that don't contain gluten. But can you trust a label? In our expose on gluten free products we found that in some instances, maybe you can't.

VO: Three shop outlets were featured in our investigation, that sold products labelled gluten-free,

Sound up: Claire: They call it food fraud, you label it one thing but you sell something else. //

VO: Carte Blanche had scientifically tested samples and found excessive amounts of gluten, from Jemi Bread, Green Valley Life and The Freedom Place. The Freedom Place in Cape Town baked their own breads and said they never claimed their goods were gluten-free.//BEAT


VO: When we first confronted One Life and Natures Healing in Centurion, they said they believed the products they were selling were gluten free. Both put the onus wholly on their suppliers.// BEAT
VO: So we checked back on these two stores to see if anything has changed. // BEAT

One Life: Let's show the breads that we have. The breads are sold, so we don’t have breads.
Mac: So there's no breads?
One life: No they're sold out. Sorry about that

VO: According to the One Life shop assistant they continue to get their products from the same supplier. (8")

Mac: Are you guys 100% sure all your breads are gluten free?
One Life: Well that's what the supplier says,then we must believe that the breads are gluten free.

VO: After revisiting One-Life, we called their supplier of Jemi Bread, Geoffrey Wainer, he said he can no longer guarantee his products are gluten-free.

Voice Recording: Jeffrey [Geoffrey Wainer, Jemi Bread.m4a 00:56 - 01:02] :
My customers know that it’s not gluten free, and I tell them it’s not gluten free

One Life: We actually put something up there at the tills to say that you buy this bread at your own risk .

VO: When we asked to see the sign the shop assistant said they had removed it but they would make an effort to put it back up. But there was still a board that advertised the breads as gluten-free. Geoffrey told us he will ask One-LIfe to take it down. // BEAT
Jason Neilson another supplier of Jemi bread was shocked when we had originally shown him our results

Sound up Jason: I'm not walking away very happy. I'm quite upset about that

VO: He passed the buck to his supplier and baker, Better Sibanda, who in turn, stated that he has never supplied anyone with "gluten free breads or products and still stands by that statement. // BEAT
VO: Since our broadcast, Jason Neilson has shut down his business Bella B and is no longer supplying any gluten-free products. // BEAT
VO: Green Valley Life also supplied products that tested high in gluten. Owner Raven Rambally has since said that this aspect of his business has ceased.
Beat// transition
VO: Our next stop was Nature's Healing. Here we met with Dr Maimoona Mahomed again.

Maimoona: In fact the company contacted us and we said we'd never buy it again.

VO: They now have a new supplier with gluten-free certification.

VO: There was still another issue we sought clarity on, as it had emerged that Dr Mahomed was not a registered naturopath which Carte Blanche brought to her attention. She was unaware that this claim was illegal and showed us her many qualifications. She now calls herself a complementary health practitioner. (14")

VO:[ding ding] But it seemed that the correct documents were not forthcoming from the University, until we made a check up call this week and the current Acting Director General of Sport and Recreation Sumayya Khan made it all happen and sent Carte Blanche proof of payment to confirm that Noni’s fees have now been settled. (24") VO: Now Noni is pursuing her dream of representing South Africa at the Olympic Games as the rules on professional participation have changed. (9)" 3. CHAOS THE LION LINK: A few months ago we came up close and personal with a 16 year old skin cancer patient - Chaos the lion from the Lory Park Zoo. He was diagnosed with cancerous lesions on his nose and foot. And In an unusual situation, he received radiation treatment from a human hospital, a South African first and Carte Blanche was there, but is he fully recovered? (22") VO: Matty Van Eck is Chaos' co-owner, she said there was no other option as no veterinary practices had the appropriate equipment. (10") Sound up Derek VO: carte blanche followed the 3rd of his 4 radiation treatments …. cost 50 000 rand … all the way to the darting of chaos with the doctor.. to that's what he thinks of me … it's a good shot (approximately 15") VO: Chaos was treated successfully with radiation therapy and some of the tumors were surgically removed. (8") Sound up Derek : A sigh of relief as Chaos blinks (5") VO: It's been a few months since his harrowing ordeal and we paid Chaos a visit to see how he is faring . (8") He greeted his co-owner Matty Van Eck followed closely by his lifelong partner Tequila Matty 00:02:16:09 – 00:02:35:25 Yes. So to protect the areas where had the treatment from the cancer reoccurring he's got to get sunblock every morning before he comes out. (11") Mac 00:01:52:20 – 00:01:58:11 How's the treatment going. Matty 00:01:58:11 – 00:02:12:13 Matty: It was a difficult decision to make because we knew how much stress and how much he was gonna have to go through it was a good decision and a good outcome. He's really doing well. (19") Mac [00:02:54.03] and is enjoying himself here with his partner. Matty 00:02:55:16 – 00:02:58:26 He is. Mac [00:02:58.20] Oh what's life without tequila? Matty [00:02:59.13] Exactly! (8") 4. RAPE KIT SHORTAGE LINK: This year the rape statistics are grimmer than ever with 41 583 reported rapes, With such alarming figures, it was touted as a national crisis when in August, Carte Blanche broke the story on a shortage of evidence collection kits including sexual assault kits, otherwise known as rape kits at police stations, due to tenders that were not awarded. We keep track of the story. (27") VO: Two weeks later we reported that the tender had been awarded and a roll out plan was scheduled. Spokesperson for the National Commissioner of Police, Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo, gives us the current status. ( 11") Vish 00:00:04:11 – 00:00:35:15 we're expecting the next delivery between the 14th and 18th of October and then followed by 27th of October to the 1st of November and then again from the 11th to the 15th of November for this year. Mac 00:00:35:07 – 00:01:00:03 would that be enough to cover most of the police stations around the country or every police station around the country? (7") Vish 00:01:00:03 – 00:01:27:26 As we stand now, we are fine. We have enough kits. VO: But Brigadier Naidoo denies that there was ever a shortage of rape kits, and says that police stations were mandated to procure rape kits from other suppliers while the tender was being awarded. Vish Naidoo: [00:12:11.07] So those figures that they were buying were not being fed into the central system. So they got the figures from that central system whereas the provinces physically had those collection kits. VO: He also states that on the 5th of August an inventory was done by Major General LInda , Head of the FCS unit and there were enough rape kits around the country. This he says averaged around 45 kits per station, but the distribution is weighted to the more densely populated precincts. Vish: [00:10:10.29] The turnaround time has to be quicker than in a rural area or outlying area. But having said that it does not mean that service delivery must be compromised. VO: But our report told a different story. (11") 01: 46 Claire A sexual assault kit like this can be the difference beween somebody being convicted and walking away scott free. Sound up: Undercover person 01:22 there's units that don't have any rape kits. Claire: Out of fear of reprisal FCS officer Thabo is hiding his identity to expose this critical shortage. Carte Blanche confirmed his story with other FCS officers and prosecutors. Sound up undercover: 2:25 - We are struggling to get kits now for the past year, especially the buccal sample to compare the DNA that was found on the victim with a suspect. VO: Brigadier Naidoo, does agree that there was a shortage of buccal swab kits, but he says, the same outcome can be achieved through taking blood samples. (12")) Vish 00:05:19:01 – 00:06:22:01 In fact that is about the first evidence collection kit that we have already taken delivery of. (13") (Beat) VO: Our story had a profound impact on one of our viewers, Penny Stein who together with the Angel Network raised R240 000 and created a rape comfort kit for victims, which includes soft toys for children and hygene products. Last week they made their first delivery at the Alexandra Clinic in Sandton. 10" 5 LIVE ANIMAL EXPORTS LINK: A few weeks ago we did an expose on the cruel conditions surrounding the transportation of livestock by sea to the Middle East from Australia. But now the company Al Mawashi who was responsible for these inhumane conditions is on South African shores and has secured a deal to ship millions of our sheep live - to the Middle East over the next few years. Will our government allow this practice to continue? (25") Sound up: Shatha Hamade The inherent suffering and risk in this trade are actually unavoidable. (5") VO: Docked on our shores The Al Shuwaikh, Al Mawashi's Cargo ship is now waiting for roughly 61 000 sheep, destined for a traumatic journey to the Middle East. (9") In our story we reported that Senior Inspector Nazareth Appalsamy with the NSPCA’s Farm Animal Protection Unit met with a representative from Al Mawashi earlier this year.(9") Sound Up Inspector: Shockingly he told us that they intend importing over the next three to 5 years 600,000 animals annually made up of sheep, goats and cattle. (9") VO: Carte Blanche had gained access to undercover footage onboard export vessels, including the Al Shuwaikh, that is so disturbing we decided it unsuitable for broadcast. sound up -[Sheep insert: 02:52] It shows sheep weak from heat exhaustion, collapsing and literally drowning in their own waste VO: Last Sunday the NSPCA undertook an inspection of the empty Al-Shuweikh vessel, and found it to be unsuitable to transport 61 000 sheep. Two inspections this week at Al-Mawashi's sheep feedlot on Page Farming Trust premises in Berlin, Eastern Cape, found a number of serious concerns. Sheep were fighting over food and no shelter was provided, amongst other cruel conditions. The Inspectors had to euthanase a total of seven sheep. VO: We tried to contact Al-Mawashi for comment on the inspections but they did not answer our calls. We were told the owners of Page Farming Trust were out of the country and unavailable for comment. The NSPCA have appealed to the South African Government to take a stand against the export of live sheep to Kuwait. (37"). 6. GLUTEN FREE FOOD LINK: Gluten has become a no no in many diets, and many people claim to be gluten intolerant, so they opt for foods - that don't contain gluten. But can you trust a label? In our expose on gluten free products we found that in some instances, maybe you can't. VO: Three shop outlets were featured in our investigation, that sold products labelled gluten-free, Sound up: Claire: They call it food fraud, you label it one thing but you sell something else. // VO: Carte Blanche had scientifically tested samples and found excessive amounts of gluten, from Jemi Bread, Green Valley Life and The Freedom Place. The Freedom Place in Cape Town baked their own breads and said they never claimed their goods were gluten-free.//BEAT VO: When we first confronted One Life and Natures Healing in Centurion, they said they believed the products they were selling were gluten free. Both put the onus wholly on their suppliers.// BEAT VO: So we checked back on these two stores to see if anything has changed. // BEAT One Life: Let's show the breads that we have. The breads are sold, so we don’t have breads. Mac: So there's no breads? One life: No they're sold out. Sorry about that VO: According to the One Life shop assistant they continue to get their products from the same supplier. (8") Mac: Are you guys 100% sure all your breads are gluten free? One Life: Well that's what the supplier says,then we must believe that the breads are gluten free. VO: After revisiting One-Life, we called their supplier of Jemi Bread, Geoffrey Wainer, he said he can no longer guarantee his products are gluten-free. Voice Recording: Jeffrey [Geoffrey Wainer, Jemi Bread.m4a 00:56 - 01:02] : My customers know that it’s not gluten free, and I tell them it’s not gluten free One Life: We actually put something up there at the tills to say that you buy this bread at your own risk . VO: When we asked to see the sign the shop assistant said they had removed it but they would make an effort to put it back up. But there was still a board that advertised the breads as gluten-free. Geoffrey told us he will ask One-LIfe to take it down. // BEAT Jason Neilson another supplier of Jemi bread was shocked when we had originally shown him our results Sound up Jason: I'm not walking away very happy. I'm quite upset about that VO: He passed the buck to his supplier and baker, Better Sibanda, who in turn, stated that he has never supplied anyone with "gluten free breads or products and still stands by that statement. // BEAT VO: Since our broadcast, Jason Neilson has shut down his business Bella B and is no longer supplying any gluten-free products. // BEAT VO: Green Valley Life also supplied products that tested high in gluten. Owner Raven Rambally has since said that this aspect of his business has ceased. Beat// transition VO: Our next stop was Nature's Healing. Here we met with Dr Maimoona Mahomed again. Maimoona: In fact the company contacted us and we said we'd never buy it again. VO: They now have a new supplier with gluten-free certification. VO: There was still another issue we sought clarity on, as it had emerged that Dr Mahomed was not a registered naturopath which Carte Blanche brought to her attention. She was unaware that this claim was illegal and showed us her many qualifications. She now calls herself a complementary health practitioner. (14")

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Over the year Carte Blanche has brought to light stories that affect the lives of ordinary South Africans but sometimes questions remain unanswered. We revisit some of them and give you an update.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Research has shown that Carte Blanche viewers want feedback on some stories that have been aired but may still have questions hanging. We revisit some of those stories and keep our viewers updated and engaged with our content.
metadata.Summary: The stories we will revisit are as follows: 1. Dusi River Chemical disaster Mark Graham from Ground Truth has been employed by Willowton to do an EIA after the chemical spillage, as Willowton have taken responsibility for the disaster, and are engaging in a rehabilitation process of the area. He will send us the update on the area. 2. Gluten free Bread We go back to the two health shops featured in the story and see if they are labelling the bread differently, we also check on Dr Maimoona’s credentials that she touts as a naturopath. 3. Rape Kits Women and men against child abuse are giving out rape comfort kits after the airing of our rape kit shortage story and they are delivering their first batch to the Alexandra Clinic in Alexandra. We will also follow up on the roll out of the actual rape kits throughout the country now that the tender has been awarded. This is within the backdrop of the GBV protests, and we can show the footage that Lezanne filmed in Sandton. 4. Lifestyle Legal Currently the class action is being instituted against Lifestyle Legal by the Stellenboch Law Clinic. Stephan Van der Merwe will provide us with an update. 5. Chaos the lion We go to the Centurion Zoo and Visit Chaos the Lion who has fully recovered from his cancer and speak to his owner, Matty Lory on his recovery. 6. Noni Tenge Noni has just retained her WBF welterweight title, and now has her eye on the Olympics, but the Department of sport has not paid the outstanding amounts for her studies at UKZN as promised on camera to Carte Blanche. We try and get some clarity from the department.
metadata.Further information: The links into the stories will be presented in a high tech way using a horizontal floating screen which has a visual block of each story, which can be tapped or swiped by the presenter and that will take us into the update.
